grpc_config.description: The full text of the Service Config YAML file (Example located here). If provided, must also provide protoc_output_base64. open_api config must not be provided.
grpc_config.rationale: The full free-form Service Config YAML for the gRPC API. Writing a generic platform policy that meaningfully constrains an arbitrary embedded document is impractical (like an IAM policy_data blob), so it is out of scope as a policy target.

openapi_config.description: The full text of the OpenAPI YAML configuration as described here. Either this, or both of grpc_config and protoc_output_base64 must be specified.
openapi_config.rationale: The full free-form OpenAPI YAML for the service. While transport security matters, it lives inside an arbitrary embedded document; a generic platform policy cannot reliably parse/constrain that blob, so like a free-form policy document it is out of scope.

project.description: The project ID that the service belongs to. If not provided, provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifier of the project the service belongs to. We do not constrain project references; enforcing an 'approved' project would require hardcoding a specific project, which is overreaching.

protoc_output_base64.description: The full contents of the Service Descriptor File generated by protoc. This should be a compiled .pb file, base64-encoded.
protoc_output_base64.rationale: A base64-encoded compiled protobuf service descriptor. It is an opaque artifact; a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain its contents without pinning a specific approved blob, so it is out of scope as a policy target.

service_name.description: The name of the service. Usually of the form $apiname.endpoints.$projectid.cloud.goog.
service_name.rationale: The name/identity of the Endpoints service. We do not constrain resource names, and enforcing an 'approved domain' would require hardcoding a specific name, which is overreaching.
